guard: a pending seed child marker whose reconcile parent is dead is repaired by the next command; a corrupt marker still fails loud
why: A service restart killed `cotal spawn` between writing the pending child marker and the child's
first act. Every later command, `ext seed --repair` included, refused with `a connector seed may
be mid-flight` until the marker was removed by hand. One mutant per promise: the classification
that calls the dead-parent marker orphaned, and the boot gate that resumes it.
Marker ownership: a child of an older reconcile must not take over or remove a newer one's marker.
Each transition runs under the marker lock, so the guard is checked in-process by
smoke:seed-checkout-store. Not proven: the lock itself serializing two real processes.

mutations.name: a pending marker with a dead parent is classified ambiguous again
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: dead-parent marker: the next command repairs and succeeds
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: dead-parent marker: the next command repairs and succeeds

mutations.name: the boot gate does not resume an orphaned seed
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: dead-parent marker: the next command repairs and succeeds
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: dead-parent marker: the next command repairs and succeeds

mutations.name: a stale child upgrades whatever marker it finds
mutations.find: if (marker?.state !== "pending" || marker.nonce !== nonce || marker.parentPid !== parentPid) return false;
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: stale child: its live upgrade against a newer reconcile's marker is refused
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: stale child: its live upgrade against a newer reconcile's marker is refused

mutations.name: a clear removes the marker whoever owns it
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: stale child: its clear leaves the newer live marker in place
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: stale child: its clear leaves the newer live marker in place
